description: Dull olive under a dark web of root, plain enough to lose in the grass. Your cuts close over and your blows come up green.
lore: Stones are weighed by hand before they are weighed by scale, and the hand is hunting appetite: a piece off something that burned sits in the palm with a want that comes through a glove. This one sits there like a stone — matte olive, no shine, easy to lose in grass — and the trade priced it accordingly for years. Wrongly. The flattest ones are not empty; their want is pointed at something other than you.

Carry one and the pointing shows: by evening the small hurts have closed unnoticed and the day's work has come apart readier than the edge explains. Everything else off a [[monsters/dark_donkey|Nightmule]] is about a person who is not there. The stone alone is about the animal, and there is no owner in it at any depth — whoever walked at the front never reached the bottom. What reached the bottom was the going on, unloaded, in a straight line. That is the part in your pocket.
